label: Richard Joyce, Moral Anti-Realism §3.3, ': In the taxonomy on which objectivism holds that moral…
locator: §3.3, '(Note that this taxonomy makes the two contraries rather than contradictories; the error theorist and the noncognitivist count as neither objectivists nor non-objectivists.'
interpretation: Read as: in the §3.3 taxonomy, objectivism and non-objectivism both say that moral facts exist, so a noncognitivist, who holds no such facts in the metaphysical sense, is neither. Applying this to quasi-realism is a reading choice: the entry presents quasi-realism as a noncognitivist program with 'an anti-realist metaphysical stance' (§3.1), though Blackburn calls his view projectivism. The claim is about objectivism as a metaphysical thesis; it does not say that a quasi-realist may not assert the mind-independence counterfactual (DISAMB-MIND-INDEPENDENCE). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the taxonomy the entry gives, not a thesis about Blackburn's own wording.
